title: A Comment Count Is Not A Reasoned Response
summary: A dependency map tracing submissions through record integrity, material-issue classification, evidence, alternatives, reasons, dissent, independent review, and appeal.
map_question: What converts a collection of public submissions into an accountable public response without treating comments as votes?
interpretation_boundary: Receipt, publication, topic tagging, deduplication, summary, sentiment, and counts do not establish materiality, evidentiary weight, response adequacy, consensus, legitimacy, or authorization.

nodes.label: Versioned public submissions and hearing records
Material-issue matrix
nodes.note: Every issue has scope, evidence, alternative, affected group, and challenge lineage.

nodes.label: Specific reasoned response
nodes.note: Reasons identify authority, evidence, uncertainty, decision effect, and residual dispute.

nodes.label: Independent completeness and conflict review
nodes.note: Omission and unsupported inference remain challengeable.

nodes.label: Closure receipt and appeal route
nodes.note: No response closure or appeal record exists.

links.note: A usable public record preserves identity and corrections appropriately.
Every material issue needs a response.

what_this_map_supports: A twelve-class issue matrix retaining submissions, evidence, responses, and dissent.
Reviewable materiality decisions and public reasons.
Independent closure and an explicit appeal path.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not establish that any comment is correct or representative.
It does not infer response adequacy from publication or process closure.
It does not create consensus, consent, legitimacy, mandate, score, or rank.
next_records_needed: An authorized process and stable common evidence record.
Actual submissions, hearings, issue classifications, challenges, and draft responses.
Independent review, closure receipt, and appeal availability.
